title: ping_l2 loopback: RX authentication fails (-200) on self-addressed signed Echo Request after reinit
description: Found while debugging vn0t (full heft trace on build-pingl2-v). After test_disable_retries completes (module RUNNING, keys re-provisioned via reprovision_after_reinit), test_full_l2_loopback_ping sends its Echo Request successfully (frame build now works post-237dc35064), the lora_loopback driver delivers it back, and lichen_l2 RX rejects it: 'RX failed: authentication failed (-200)' at [00:00:220]. The frame is signed by the node's own test key and the peer table holds the same (eui64, test_pubkey) via lichen_peer_add, so verify should pass. Candidate causes to check: (1) peer-table entry cleared on disable and re-added with a DIFFERENT eui64 byte order than the frame's source address; (2) epoch/nonce mismatch after epoch_advance_for_boot on the reinit path (RX replay/window check misfiring as EAUTH); (3) reprovision lichen_l2_test_load_key returning -EALREADY on the second call leaving an OLD key active while the peer holds the new pubkey (helper tolerates -EALREADY); (4) SCHC decompress altering the authenticated transcript. This blocks test_full_l2_loopback_ping (10s packet-path wait times out).
close_reason: Root cause: the test registered its self peer under the DEVICE synthetic hardware EUI-64, but frame SIIDs are the canonical key-derived EUI-64 (lichen_link_tx.c derive_signer_eui64: sha512(pubkey)[0:8] with U/L set) and peer lookup is SIID-indexed (lichen_l2_peer.c:202 peer_find_locked(signer_iid)) -> miss -> -LICHEN_EAUTH. Fix (24cde81e5a): register the peer under the canonical form in ping_l2_setup AND reprovision_after_reinit (lichen_pubkey_to_iid + |=0x02, byte-exact with the tx/rx derivations per review pass 1). Validated on heft (main + test file + l2_tx capacity fix copied): test_full_l2_loopback_ping now PASSES — the full TX->loopback->RX-auth->reply path runs; suite 6/7. The last failure (test_udp_payload...) is NOT auth: it is the recv_async re-arm EBUSY abort tracked in 17nw (loopback driver keeps the callback registered across deliveries while the RX layer re-arms after each delivery). Reviews: 3 passes on kimi-k3 — correctness PASS, security PASS (production auth unaffected; verify still fails closed on bad signatures), edge PASS (one style nit fixed: blank line restored).
